items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I also saw and talked with a man I had known about and admired when I was very young. He was the ex-heavyweight boxing champion of the world, Jack Johnson.

ctx.x: drummer, Eugene Anderson, piano, Booker T. Pittman, Leroy Hardy, alto sax, Alfred Pratt, tenor sax.

Duke Ellington was playing some exclusive place in a suburb of Chicago and I saw Freddie Jenkins and Rex Stewart many times. The fattest musician I ever saw was also in Chicago. His name was Tiny Parham and he played piano. He had an orchestra but I never heard it. I did, however, see his car in which he had had the steering wheel put almost in the middle of the front seat in order for him to drive it. I thought that the tuba player with Broadus was the biggest, fattest mucisian I had ever seen until I saw Tiny…

From Chicago we went to Cleveland at the R.K.O. Theater for one week and from there to Denver, Colorado which was the farthest west I had ever been. We played the R.K.O. vaudeville theater and visited the Rocky Mountains.
